This is a test post to confirm that R chunks run and plots render.

## The data

The built-in `mtcars` dataset has fuel economy and design figures for 32 cars.

### Summary statistics


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data(mtcars)
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      mpg              wt              hp       
 Min.   :10.40   Min.   :1.513   Min.   : 52.0  
 1st Qu.:15.43   1st Qu.:2.581   1st Qu.: 96.5  
 Median :19.20   Median :3.325   Median :123.0  
 Mean   :20.09   Mean   :3.217   Mean   :146.7  
 3rd Qu.:22.80   3rd Qu.:3.610   3rd Qu.:180.0  
 Max.   :33.90   Max.   :5.424   Max.   :335.0  
```


:::
:::


### Correlations


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
round(cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")]), 2)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      mpg    wt    hp
mpg  1.00 -0.87 -0.78
wt  -0.87  1.00  0.66
hp  -0.78  0.66  1.00
```


:::
:::


## A plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#3c5c3a", size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "#a86f1a", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Fuel economy falls as vehicle weight rises.](index_files/figure-html/fig-mpg-wt-1.png){#fig-mpg-wt width=672}
:::
:::


## A simple model


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
summary(fit)$coefficients
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
               Estimate Std. Error   t value     Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) 37.22727012 1.59878754 23.284689 2.565459e-20
wt          -3.87783074 0.63273349 -6.128695 1.119647e-06
hp          -0.03177295 0.00902971 -3.518712 1.451229e-03
```


:::
:::


## Wrapping up

If you can see the code, its output, and the plot above, Quarto and R are wired up correctly.
